pages.title: Four Labour Codes come into force

facts.text: Effective: 21 November 2025 — 4 Labour Codes replace 29 Central labour laws
facts.head: News

facts.text: Labour: in Concurrent List (Entries 22–24, 35, List III)
facts.head: News

facts.text: Code: Code on Wages, 2019; Laws merged: 4
facts.head: News

facts.text: Code: Code on Social Security, 2020; Laws merged: 9 (EPF, ESI, gratuity, maternity benefit)
facts.head: News

facts.text: Code: Industrial Relations Code, 2020; Laws merged: 3 (Trade Unions, Industrial Disputes, Industrial Employment)
facts.head: News

facts.text: Code: OSH Code, 2020; Laws merged: 13 (factories, mines, contract labour, construction)
facts.head: News

facts.text: Applies to all employees; National Floor Wage — States cannot fix minimum wage below it
facts.head: Code on Wages

facts.text: Wage = Basic + DA + Retaining Allowance; deductions max 50%
facts.head: Code on Wages

facts.text: Hours: 8–12/day, max 48/week; overtime at least 2x
facts.head: Code on Wages

facts.text: Payment: monthly within 7 days; on resignation/termination within 2 days; mandatory wage slips
facts.head: Code on Wages

facts.text: ⚠ First time legal definition of gig and platform workers; Social Security Fund
facts.head: Code on Social Security

facts.text: Aggregators: contribute 1–2% of annual turnover, capped at 5% of amount payable to gig workers
facts.head: Code on Social Security

facts.text: Fixed-term employees: ⚠ gratuity after 1 year (earlier 5 years for permanent)
facts.head: Code on Social Security

facts.text: EPFO: establishments with 20+ employees; ESIC: pan-India, mandatory even with 1 worker in hazardous work (earlier 10)
facts.head: Code on Social Security

facts.text: Inspector-cum-facilitators replace inspectors
facts.head: Code on Social Security

facts.text: Worker includes supervisory staff earning < ₹18,000/month
facts.head: Industrial Relations Code

facts.text: ⚠ Layoff/retrenchment/closure permission threshold: 100 → 300 workers
facts.head: Industrial Relations Code

facts.text: Strike: notice within 60 days before; no strike within 14 days of notice; mass casual leave by >50% workers = strike
facts.head: Industrial Relations Code

facts.text: Negotiating union: 51% membership; council — unions with ≥20%
facts.head: Industrial Relations Code

facts.text: Factory licence: with power 10 → 20 workers; without power 20 → 40
facts.head: OSH Code

facts.text: Contract labour: applies when contractor has 50+ (earlier 20)
facts.head: OSH Code

facts.text: Women: may work before 6 am / after 7 pm with consent and safety
facts.head: OSH Code

facts.text: Mandatory appointment letters; annual free health check
facts.head: OSH Code

facts.text: Safety Committees: ≥500 factory, ≥250 construction, ≥100 mine workers
facts.head: OSH Code

facts.text: Notified: 14 November 2025 — operationalise the DPDP Act, 2023 (passed August 2023)
facts.head: News

facts.text: Draft Rules: released January 2025
facts.head: News

facts.text: Immediate effect: formation of Data Protection Board of India (DPBI) + the RTI amendment
facts.head: News

facts.text: Phased: most provisions apply after 12–18 months (consent system, erasure, DPOs, audits, breach reporting — 2026–27)
facts.head: News

facts.text: Citizen rights: erasure, correction, grievance redressal, appoint digital nominee (after death/incapacity)
facts.head: Key features

facts.text: Consent: informed consent; withdrawal as easy as giving; Consent Managers
facts.head: Key features

facts.text: Children: targeted ads restricted; limited exemption for parents to track child's location
facts.head: Key features

facts.text: Significant Data Fiduciaries (SDFs): graded obligations
facts.head: Key features

facts.text: DPBI: "digital by design" — works as a digital office; online complaints; can drop proceedings on a voluntary undertaking
facts.head: Key features

facts.text: ⚠ DPBI is a subordinate office of MeitY (criticised for lack of independence)
facts.head: Key features

facts.text: ⚠ Section 8(1)(j) of RTI Act, 2005 — the public interest override for personal information removed
facts.head: RTI amendment

facts.text: Term: Data Principal; Meaning: Individual whose data is processed
facts.head: Background

facts.text: Term: Data Fiduciary; Meaning: Entity deciding purpose and means of processing
facts.head: Background

facts.text: Puttaswamy (2017): privacy a fundamental right under Article 21
facts.head: Background

facts.text: Srikrishna Committee draft — 2018
facts.head: Background

pages.title: Chandigarh under Article 240 — Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill, 2025

facts.text: Proposal: Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill, 2025 to add Chandigarh to Article 240
facts.head: News

facts.text: Backlash: in Punjab (AAP CM Bhagwant Mann, Congress, SAD, Punjab BJP chief Sunil Jakhar)
facts.head: News

facts.text: MHA clarified: no final decision; ⚠ no Bill in Winter Session 2025
facts.head: News

facts.text: Effect if passed: independent Administrator/L-G; President could make regulations for Chandigarh
facts.head: News

facts.text: President makes regulations for "peace, progress and good government" of UTs: A&N Islands, Lakshadweep, DNH & DD, Puducherry (certain conditions)
facts.head: Article 240

facts.text: Regulation has force of an Act of Parliament; can amend/repeal Parliament's laws for that UT
facts.head: Article 240

facts.text: Fact: UT + joint capital; Detail: Of Punjab and Haryana — Punjab Reorganisation Act, 1966 (passed 18 Sep 1966)
facts.head: Chandigarh status

facts.text: Fact: Haryana; Detail: 17th state
facts.head: Chandigarh status

facts.text: Fact: Administrator; Detail: ⚠ Governor of Punjab (since 1984) — not Haryana Governor
facts.head: Chandigarh status

facts.text: Fact: Property split; Detail: ⚠ 60:40 (Punjab:Haryana)
facts.head: Chandigarh status

facts.text: Fact: Capital law; Detail: Capital of Punjab (Development and Regulation) Act, 1952
facts.head: Chandigarh status

facts.text: Fact: Periphery; Detail: Punjab New Capital (Periphery) Control Act, 1952 — 16 km radius
facts.head: Chandigarh status

facts.text: Fact: Became Punjab capital; Detail: 1953, inaugurated by President Rajendra Prasad
facts.head: Chandigarh status

facts.text: Fact: Land; Detail: 22 villages of Kharar
facts.head: Chandigarh status

facts.text: Fact: 1970 (29 January); Detail: Centre said Chandigarh should go to Punjab as a whole
facts.head: Chandigarh status

facts.text: Fact: 2016; Detail: Attempt to appoint K. J. Alphons as Administrator shelved
facts.head: Chandigarh status

pages.title: Cannabis cultivation vs bhang — Kerala HC on NDPS Act

facts.text: Kerala High Court (4 Nov 2025): dismissed plea of a man caught with five cannabis plants on terrace
facts.head: News

facts.text: Ruling: cultivation of any cannabis plant is illegal even with no flowering/fruiting tops; includes keeping in pots
facts.head: News

facts.text: Term: Charas; Meaning: Resin of cannabis (incl. hashish oil)
facts.head: NDPS Act, 1985 — definitions

facts.text: Term: Ganja; Meaning: Flowering or fruiting tops (contain THC)
facts.head: NDPS Act, 1985 — definitions

facts.text: Term: Excluded; Meaning: Leaves and seeds without flowering tops
facts.head: NDPS Act, 1985 — definitions

facts.text: Term: Cannabis plant — Section 2(iv); Meaning: Any plant of genus cannabis, irrespective of age/flowering
facts.head: NDPS Act, 1985 — definitions

facts.text: ⚠ Bhang is made from leaves — not a narcotic under NDPS; States regulate it (UP, Rajasthan licensed shops; Assam bans it)
facts.head: NDPS Act, 1985 — definitions

facts.text: Section 8(b): prohibits cultivation of any cannabis plant without approval
facts.head: NDPS Act, 1985 — definitions

facts.text: Section 14: Govt may allow cultivation for industrial (hemp), horticultural, medical/scientific use
facts.head: NDPS Act, 1985 — definitions

facts.text: Item: Ganja; Small quantity: up to 1 kg — jail up to 1 year, fine up to ₹10,000; Commercial quantity: 20 kg+ — 10–20 years, fine ₹1–2 lakh
facts.head: Punishments

facts.text: Item: Charas; Small quantity: up to 100 g; Commercial quantity: 1 kg+
facts.head: Punishments

facts.text: Cultivation: up to 10 years RI and ₹1 lakh fine
facts.head: Punishments

facts.text: Industrial hemp: ⚠ Uttarakhand first to issue licences (2018); also UP, HP, MP
facts.head: Background

facts.text: India's first medical cannabis clinic: Bengaluru (2020)
facts.head: Background

facts.text: UN Commission on Narcotic Drugs: founded 1946, HQ Vienna
facts.head: Background

facts.text: Recreational use legal: Canada, Uruguay, 15 US states; 50+ countries allow medicinal cannabis
facts.head: Background

facts.text: Delhi HC hearing challenge by Great Legalisation Movement India Trust
facts.head: Background

facts.text: NDPS Act enacted under international pressure, mainly USA
facts.head: Background
